newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on CBOT soybean spillover.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on CBOT soybean spillover.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher on spillover support from CBOT soybeans, which closed at or near their upper trading limits on fund buying, traders said.
The 30-cent-per-bushel limit-up move in CBOT May, July, August and Sept soybeans helped trigger some minor buy stops in KCBT May wheat, traders said.
"There was no real action late other than soybean spillover, and there was no real action early other than locals jockeying for position ahead of tomorrow's report," a KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat settled two to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with May up 2-3/4 cents at $4.12-1/4. July gained 3-1/2 cents to settle at $3.77-1/4, and March gained 3-1/4 cent to close at $4.38-3/4.
Traders said Wolcott Lincoln and Prudential Securities each bought at least 1.2 million July bushels.
